title: client-capability-probe-catalog
content:
Purpose:
- Capture a lightweight catalogue of client -> server capability probes and a minimal protocol sketch for feature negotiation and graceful degradation.
- Goal: standardize the first-touch behaviour from SDKs/clients so hosted/dedicated/private control planes can make safe routing, billing, and fallback decisions without heavy coupling.

Motivation / contexts I've bumped into:
- mobile/web SDKs need to know if the endpoint supports: streaming, function-calling, low-latency optimized variants, token-cost-estimates, structured-output enforcement, or local-offline-fallback tokens.
- Server can have multiple model variants (fp16, int8, quantized, short-seq-optimized) and different SLA tiers. Preflight probe avoids sending a large request only to find unsupported features.
- Avoid tight coupling: keep probes minimal, idempotent, cheap, and cacheable for short TTLs.

Constraints / desiderata:
- Minimal bytes on first request; work for high-latency or metered networks.
- Backwards-compatible: unknown fields are ignored.
- Cacheable at client and intermediary (CDN/gateway) with TTL.
- Privacy: no user data in probe payloads.
- Allow server to advertise experimental feature flags and targetable rollout tokens.

Probe shapes (sketches) - return and request are JSON-like but actual SDKs will wrap HTTP headers when possible. Keep kebab-case keys.

1) Minimal probe request (fast, cacheable)
- HTTP POST /v1/capability-probe or HTTP OPTIONS /v1/generate with Accept-Capabilities header (alternatives).
- body: { "client-id": <client-sdk-id>, "sdk-version": "1.4.0", "probe": ["streaming","func-call","short-seq-opt"] }
- headers: X-Redwood-Probe: 1, X-Client-Region: us-west-2 (optional)

Example request body (stringified):
{
  "client-id": "web-sdk@1.4.0",
  "probe": ["streaming","func-calls","token-estimates"],
  "transport-hints": ["http2","websocket"]
}

2) Full capability catalog response (server)
- body: {
  "capabilities": ["streaming","func-calls","structured-output"],
  "variants": {"short-seq-opt": {"supported": true, "latency-ms": 30}},
  "fallback-policy": "downgrade-to-short-seq-opt",
  "ttl_seconds": 60,
  "rollout_token": "canary-3"
}

Notes: all fields optional; unknown fields ignored. ttl_seconds controls client cache. rollout_token used by SDK to tag subsequent requests for telemetry and targeting.

3) Lightweight header-only exchange (for web/CDN friendly)
- Request: OPTIONS /v1/generate with header Accept-Capabilities: streaming,func-calls
- Response headers: X-Redwood-Capabilities: streaming,func-calls
- X-Redwood-Cap-TTL: 60

4) Fallback-policy enum (server hints clients how to degrade)
- none: server expects client to handle errors (default)
- retry-with-variant: server will attempt to execute with an alternative variant and return TTL/variant hints
- downgrade: server requests client to use a cheaper model variant for this session
- redirect: server returns a redirect to a dedicated endpoint (rare, sticky)

Client state machine (sketch) - ascii flow:

[START] --(probe cached?)--> [USE CACHED CAPS] --(ok)--> [SEND MAIN REQUEST]
     |
     No
     v
   [SEND PROBE] --(200 Caps)--> [CACHE]--> [SEND MAIN REQUEST]
     |(4xx/5xx)
     v
   [Fallback policy: conservative] --> [Send best-effort main request without streaming, set telemetry flag "probe_failed"]

Edge cases:
- probe slow/unavailable: treat as transient and fall back to conservative defaults after timeout (e.g., 1500ms).
- negative cache: servers may set ttl_seconds=0 to force re-probe on each request (expensive, but used during rollouts).
- differing control planes (hosted vs private): private deployments may return more capabilities but also may not want to advertise internal flags — add "advertise_public_only": true boolean.

Config sketch for SDK (pseudo-toml-ish)
[probe]
enabled = true
endpoint = "/v1/capability-probe"
timeout_ms = 1200
cache_ttl_default = 30
prefer_header_mode = true

[fallback]
strategy = "conservative" # conservative | optimistic | aggressive
max_probe_retries = 1

Telemetry and metrics to collect (client & server) - help Ops tune TTL, timeouts, and rollout window:
- client_probe_latency_ms (histogram)
- client_probe_success (counter)
- client_probe_cached_hit (counter)
- probe_induced_fallback_count (counter)
- server_capability_variants_seen (set tag)
- correlation with request-level errors (did probe reduce 4xx/5xx?)

Security / privacy notes:
- probe must not include user PII. Only SDK id, transport hints, and anonymous region tags.
- rollout_token is ephemeral; servers should issue short-lived tokens.
- probes should not be used as an auth bypass — a probe response doesn’t imply request authorization.

Testing matrix (ideas):
- CDN mode: header-only probes through edge -> ensure TTL respected by edge caches (simulate stale behavior).
- High-latency mobile: set timeout low and verify conservative fallback path triggers.
- Canary rollout: set ttl_seconds small and ensure clients pick up new rollout_token within expected window.

Open questions / TODOs (short):
- Do we prefer header-only OPTIONS flow by default? Pros: CDN-friendly, small. Cons: limited expressivity.
- How to sign/validate rollout_token without blowing up complexity for private installs? HSM/KMS? Maybe have server-signed opaque token with short expiry.
- Should SDKs expose an explicit API for querying capabilities vs. probe-on-first-request? (both. default: probe-on-first-request with opt-in explicit query).
- Backpressure: if many clients probe aggressively, will gateways suffer? Add rate-limits or require lightweight proofs.

Next steps: (for my sprint notes)
- [ ] implement header mode toggle in web-sdk (Ravi)
- [ ] add server capability endpoint in runtime (PR referenced above)
- [ ] write integration test that simulates edge cache TTL (Sofia)
- [ ] sketch telemetry dashboard (probe latency, cache hits)

Appendix: sample minimal SDK usage (JS pseudo)
// first call will perform probe behind the scenes if needed
const cli = RedwoodSDK({ apiKey, preferHeaderMode: true });
await cli.generate({ prompt: "hi", onStream: (t)=>{/* */} });

// explicit query
const caps = await cli.queryCapabilities();
if (caps.capabilities.includes('streaming')) {
  // enable streaming path
}

-- end of draft --

Notes to self: keep this small & incremental. Aim for compatibility with existing rollout infra; don't invent heavy new tokens unless required.
